transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, doc, I'm here because... honestly, things have just been getting weird with me lately. I work down at the shipping warehouse, inventory mostly, and let me tell you, the new barcode scanners they brought in last month are a complete nightmare. You scan a pallet and half the time it doesn't even register, so you're standing there while the forklift drivers are honking at you and holding up the whole loading dock. It really messes up your whole shift. 

But anyway, what really worries me, what actually brought me in here, is what happens when I finally get home. Late at night, I start picking at food in the kitchen. And I tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' you know? But my hand... it just keeps going back. It's like I don't get to make the decision anymore. My buddy Mike at the warehouse says I just need to buy a padlock for the cabinets, but Mike also thinks he can fix his own truck transmission, and last week it broke down right on the interstate, so I'm definitely not taking advice from him. But yeah, the food thing is why I'm here.
When you're picking at the food late at night, does it feel like you can't stop, even if you want to?

Yeah, exactly. It's exactly like that. I'll be standing there in the kitchen, and I'll actually say it out loud, 'That's enough, Santiago.' But then... I don't know, my hand just keeps grabbing more. It's like my brain says stop, but my body just ignores it. It's the weirdest feeling, like I'm not even the one making the choice anymore. 

Kind of reminds me of this forklift we used to have at the warehouse, old number four. The brakes on that thing were completely shot. You'd press down on the pedal, trying to stop, and it would just keep rolling right toward the loading dock edge. Terrifying. We kept telling the floor manager, Gary, that it was a safety hazard, but Gary's one of those guys who only cares about the numbers, you know? He's always talking about 'efficiency metrics' and 'throughput,' whatever that means. Anyway, it took Jimmy actually bumping into a stack of pallets and knocking over like, three hundred boxes of packing tape before they finally retired old number four. But yeah, that's what it feels like with the food. I'm pressing the brakes, but I just keep going.
When you're picking at the food late at night, does it give you any kind of relief or pleasure, or does it just feel frustrating and out of your control?

Well, it's... it's definitely not relief. I mean, maybe for like a split second when I first start, but mostly it's just really frustrating. It's exactly like you said, completely out of my control. And then I just feel awful about myself afterward. 

It's sort of like... well, speaking of feeling awful, did I mention they changed the break room coffee at work? Used to be this decent dark roast, kept you going through the graveyard shift. Now it's this cheap, powdery stuff that tastes like burnt cardboard. Gary claims it's to cut costs, but I swear half the crew is falling asleep on their feet now. And when you're driving a forklift, falling asleep is a real bad idea. My buddy Mike actually nodded off once and almost drove right into the supervisor's office. Man, the look on Gary's face... he was yelling so loud you could hear him over the conveyor belts. But yeah, the food thing. It's just frustrating. I don't feel good about it at all.
Has this behavior with the food late at night caused you any problems at work, with your friends, or at home?

Well, work is... work is fine. I'm still getting to all my shifts at the warehouse, handling the inventory, not missing any time. Though honestly, it's a miracle anyone makes it to work on time with the construction on Route 9. Have you driven down that way recently? They've had it down to one lane for three months. Three months! They put up these orange barrels and then you never actually see anyone working. Just a bunch of guys in hard hats drinking coffee—probably that same terrible coffee Gary buys for us. I swear, if I have to sit behind another gravel truck going ten miles an hour... 

But, uh, where was I? Oh, right, the food thing. Yeah, so work is okay, but at home... it's getting a little weird. My sister and her kids are staying with me right now, and usually we all hang out in the kitchen late, playing cards or whatever. But lately, I've just been... avoiding it. I'll make an excuse and go to my room because I'm just so on edge around the food, and I'm terrified one of them is going to notice how uneasy I am. My nephew, Leo, he's a smart kid, he notices everything. Last week he asked me why I was staring at the pantry door. Kids, right? They just say whatever pops into their head. Reminds me of when I was his age, I used to ask my dad why he was going bald, which he did not appreciate. But yeah, I'm just trying to stay out of the kitchen when people are around so they don't see how weird I'm acting.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy lately?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless or anything. I mean, I'm not depressed. I still like doing my usual stuff, you know? Like watching the game on Sundays. Though honestly, the way the team is playing this year, it's a wonder anybody still watches. Did you see that fumble in the fourth quarter last week? Unbelievable. My buddy Mike—the one who almost drove the forklift into the office—he actually threw his hat at the TV. He's got this lucky hat, this old faded green thing he's had since high school, and he just chucked it right at the screen. I told him, 'Mike, you're gonna break the plasma, and Gary's not paying us enough to replace that.' 

But anyway, yeah, I'm not feeling down or losing interest in things. I still like my weekends, even if the football is terrible right now. It's really just this... this whole food thing at night that's bothering me. Everything else is pretty much normal.
Before you start picking at the food in the kitchen, do you ever feel a strong urge or a strange sensation that builds up inside you, like a need that has to be satisfied?

No, not really. I don't feel any weird build-up or anything like that. It's not like an itch I have to scratch, you know? It's just... I'm there, and then it's happening. 

Speaking of scratching an itch, though, my dog Buster has been driving me up the wall lately. He's this Golden Retriever mix, right? Great dog, usually super chill. But the last couple of weeks, he's been scratching at the back door non-stop. Like, all night long. Scratch, scratch, scratch. I thought maybe he had fleas or something, but the vet said he's clean. Turns out, there's this raccoon that's been getting into the trash cans behind the garage. Huge thing, looks like it's been eating better than half the guys at the warehouse. Mike saw it the other day when he came over to watch the game and he swore it was a small bear. But yeah, Buster just sits there at the glass door, whining and pawing at it because he wants to go out and get the raccoon. It's driving me crazy. I've had to start leaving the TV on just to drown out the noise. 

But no, I don't get any kind of urge or sensation like that before the food thing. It just kind of happens.
Before you start picking at the food, do you feel any kind of physical tension in your body or a racing, restless feeling in your mind?

No, I don't think my mind is racing... and I don't really get tense. Well, I mean, my shoulders and lower back are always a little tense, but that's just from the warehouse. You try unloading a shipment of brake pads when the main forklift is down. Which happens all the time now because Gary refuses to hire a real mechanic. He actually brought in his brother-in-law last week, this guy Steve, who supposedly knows engines. Steve spent four hours staring at the hydraulic lift, drank three of my Mountain Dews out of the breakroom fridge, and then told us we just needed to let it warm up longer in the mornings. Just total nonsense. I told Mike I'm putting a padlock on my lunch cooler next time Steve is in the building. 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, tension. No, I don't feel restless or physically tense right before I start eating. It's not like that.
Do you ever feel like you shouldn't be doing this late-night eating, and if so, do you try to stop yourself from doing it?

Yeah, I definitely feel like I shouldn't be doing it. That's the part that really worries me. Because once I start picking at the food in the kitchen, I'll literally tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago, time for bed,' but my hand just keeps going back. It's like I don't even get to make the decision anymore, you know? 

It's kind of like how Gary is about the overtime schedule at work. He says he's making the schedule, but really, his wife is the one pulling the strings. She comes into the office on Thursdays—always wearing these loud, clanky bracelets—and suddenly all the shifts are changed around. Last Thursday, she completely messed up my weekend rotation. I was supposed to have Saturday off to go to my niece's quinceañera. My sister went all out for it, rented this huge hall down by the river. They even had a chocolate fountain, which honestly sounded like a disaster waiting to happen with all those kids running around. I told my sister, 'Maria, you're gonna be cleaning chocolate off those rented chair covers for a week.' But anyway, Gary's wife just crossed my name right off the Saturday off-list. I had to threaten to use my sick days just to get out of there by three. 

But yeah, with the food, I try to stop. I tell myself to stop. But it's like my hand has a mind of its own and just keeps grabbing more.
Do you ever wake up in the middle of the night and realize you're eating without being fully aware of it?

No, I'm definitely awake. I mean, I know what I'm doing, I just... I can't seem to stop it once it starts. But I'm not sleepwalking or anything like that. 

My cousin Hector used to sleepwalk when we were kids. It was the craziest thing. He'd get up out of bed, eyes wide open but just totally blank, you know? One time, we were staying at our abuela's house for the summer, and he got up in the middle of the night, walked right past me on the top bunk, went down the hall, and started trying to unlock the front door with a spoon. A spoon! My abuela heard the rattling and came out with her broom, thinking someone was trying to break in. She almost whacked him over the head before she realized it was just Hector in his Spider-Man pajamas. After that, she started putting a chair in front of the door at night. She said it was for the sleepwalking, but I'm pretty sure she was just paranoid about the neighborhood. It was changing a lot back then. A lot of new families moving in, the old bakery on the corner closed down... man, they had the best pan dulce. You could smell it from three blocks away on a Sunday morning. 

But yeah, no, I'm awake when I'm in the kitchen. I don't wake up mid-chew or anything. I'm fully aware I'm doing it, even if I feel like I can't stop.
Does this late-night eating ever make you feel so distressed that it affects your ability to focus at work or interact with your family at home?

Well, it doesn't really affect my work. I mean, I'm still getting to all my shipping and receiving shifts on time and handling my responsibilities. You know, unloading the trucks, doing the inventory counts. Even with Gary breathing down my neck about the new barcode scanners. He bought these cheap scanners online instead of going through the corporate vendor, and half the time they don't even read the labels. I told him, 'Gary, you're trying to save a buck, but it's costing us hours in manual entry.' And don't even get me started on the battery life. You leave one off the charger for ten minutes and it's dead. Last Tuesday, I had a whole pallet of wiper blades sitting on the dock for an hour because I had to keep swapping out scanners. It's ridiculous. 

But, um, at home... yeah, it's starting to mess with things a little. I've actually started avoiding some of the late family time in the kitchen. Usually, my wife and kids will hang out there after dinner, maybe have some tea or something, but I just... I don't want to be in there. I'm worried someone will notice how uneasy I am around the food, you know? Like they'll see me eyeing the leftovers or getting anxious about it. So I just make an excuse and go watch TV in the other room.
Do you ever feel guilty or ashamed about the late-night eating, like you're doing something you shouldn't even when you're alone?

Oh, absolutely. The guilt is... it's a lot. I really don't like anyone seeing how much I put away, so I always wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are completely asleep, and I try to keep it as quiet as possible in the kitchen. 

My aunt actually just moved into our spare room downstairs a few months ago, and she is such a light sleeper. She leaves her door cracked open because of her little dog, Chico. He's this tiny Chihuahua mix that just shakes all the time, you know the type? My brother-in-law had to give him to us because his new landlord was super strict about no pets. That landlord was a real piece of work, actually. He tried to keep my brother-in-law's entire security deposit, claiming the dog ruined the carpets, but man, those carpets were from like 1992. They had that terrible green and pink floral pattern that everyone used to have in their dining rooms back in the day. I told him he should take the guy to small claims court, but he said it wasn't worth the filing fee and taking time off work. 

But anyway, Chico barks at the drop of a hat, so I have to be like a ninja with the pantry and the fridge door. If the rubber seal on the fridge makes that loud popping sound when it opens, I just freeze and hold my breath. I just... I'd be so incredibly embarrassed if she or my wife walked in and saw all the wrappers on the counter.
Before you start picking at the food, do you ever feel a specific urge, need, or pressure in your body or mind that something has to happen, even if you can’t explain why?

No, I don't think so. It's not like a pressure or an urge like that. I just... I go in there and start eating. It's not this big buildup or anything. 

Speaking of pressure, though, the tire pressure light in my truck has been driving me crazy all week. It's a 2014 Silverado, and I swear those sensors are just designed to break. I took it to the gas station down the street—the one on Elm, with the really good breakfast tacos in the back? Man, the lady who makes the salsa there, she doesn't mess around. It's got this smoky flavor, maybe chipotle or something, and it will clear your sinuses right out. I try to get there before 7:00 AM on my way to the warehouse, otherwise the line is out the door with all the construction guys working on that new apartment complex over by the highway. They're throwing those buildings up so fast, it makes you wonder about the quality, you know? Like, are the walls just paper-thin? 

But yeah, I filled all four tires, checked them with my own gauge, and the stupid light on the dashboard is still on. My buddy Dave says I just need to reset the computer, but I don't want to mess with the battery terminals and end up locking out my radio. That happened to him, and he had to drive around in silence for a month until he found the factory code in his glovebox. 

But no, to answer your question, there's no weird physical urge or anything before I eat. I just do it.
Before you start picking at the food, do you ever feel a strong internal pressure or discomfort that seems to demand you act on it, even if you don't want to?

No, like I was saying, it's really not like that. There's no pressure or discomfort or anything demanding I do it. I just... I just go to the kitchen and eat. I don't really know how else to explain it. 

But man, talking about discomfort, I slept on my neck wrong two nights ago, and I have had this knot right at the base of my skull that will not quit. My wife told me I need to get one of those contoured memory foam pillows, but I don't trust them. We bought a memory foam mattress topper a few years ago, supposedly infused with cooling gel, right? Spent like two hundred bucks on it at Bed Bath & Beyond before they closed down the one near the mall. Which is a shame, by the way, because that plaza is just dying now. The anchor store is empty, the pretzel place is gone, and the only thing left is a discount shoe store and a cell phone repair kiosk. It's depressing to drive by. 

Anyway, that mattress topper was like sleeping on a giant marshmallow that trapped all your body heat. I woke up sweating every single night in November. I finally rolled it up and shoved it in the hall closet, and it's been taking up half the space in there ever since. But yeah, no, I don't get any weird internal pressure before I eat. I just start eating.
When you're in the kitchen picking at the food, do you feel like you have to do it in order to relieve some kind of uncomfortable thought or feeling, even if it doesn't make sense?

No, I don't think it's about relieving anything. I mean, I'm not trying to make a bad thought go away or anything like that. I just... I'm just hungry, or I just want it, I guess. 

But, you know, talking about uncomfortable thoughts... my brother-in-law, the one who gave us Chico? He just called me yesterday, completely stressed out. He works for this HVAC company, and they've been doing all the ductwork for that new commercial park going up on the east side of town. Well, apparently, their supplier sent the wrong size vents for an entire floor, and the general contractor is threatening to hold their payment. It's a huge mess. He was asking if I knew anyone at my warehouse who could source the right parts faster, but our inventory is completely different. We mostly handle industrial fasteners and heavy-duty shelving units. You wouldn't believe how heavy some of those pallets are. Last week, the forklift driver, Gary—great guy, but a little careless sometimes—he clipped the edge of a rack, and I thought the whole aisle was going to come down like dominoes. Luckily, it just dented the support beam, but the safety manager had a complete meltdown. We had to sit through a two-hour safety refresher in the breakroom, and the AC in there has been broken since July. 

But yeah, no, I don't eat to relieve any weird thoughts or feelings. It's just eating.
Before you start picking at the food in the kitchen, do you ever feel an uncomfortable sensation in your body that makes you want to start eating, even if you're not exactly sure why?

No, doc, I really don't. I don't get any kind of physical feeling or uncomfortable sensation before I start eating. I just... I just go and do it. It's not like my stomach is twisting or my skin is crawling or anything weird like that. 

Speaking of crawling, though, my wife found a spider the size of a half-dollar in the garage this morning. I'm telling you, it was massive. Brown, kind of hairy. She completely freaked out, dropped the recycling bin right there on the concrete. There were cans everywhere. We usually take the cans down to the recycling center on Saturdays because they actually pay you a few cents a pound for aluminum, and it adds up, you know? Last year we saved enough from just cans to buy a new gas grill for the patio. It's a Weber, really nice one, three burners. We had the neighbors over for burgers a couple of weekends ago to break it in. 

But anyway, she's screaming about this spider, and I had to go out there with a broom. I'm not really a bug guy myself, but you gotta do what you gotta do. I ended up just sweeping it out the side door into the bushes. Hopefully it stays out there. But yeah, to get back to what you were asking... no, there's no physical feeling before I eat. I just eat.

When you're picking at the food late at night, does it usually happen in a set period of time — like within a couple of hours — and then you stop for the night, or does it just kind of happen off and on throughout the night?

Well, it's usually just in one go, you know? Like, within an hour or two. I'll get home from work, and on some nights, I can go through several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, some tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left over. And I'm just standing there in the kitchen, like I'm just cleaning up the leftovers, right? 

But speaking of leftovers, my wife makes the best pozole. She uses this specific kind of hominy she gets from the Mexican market two towns over. The one near us closed down during the pandemic, which really sucked because they had this amazing bakery inside. You could get fresh pan dulce every morning. I used to stop there on my way to the warehouse and grab a concha and a coffee. Gary, the forklift driver I mentioned? He used to beg me to bring him those little pig-shaped cookies they made. What are they called... marranitos, yeah. He loved those things. He's actually retiring next year, Gary is. Moving down to Florida to live near his daughter. I don't know how he's gonna handle the humidity down there, honestly. The warehouse gets hot, sure, but Florida is a whole different beast. 

But yeah, anyway, the eating thing... it's just in that one chunk of time, standing in the kitchen. I don't keep waking up all night to do it.
Before you start picking at the food in the kitchen, do you ever feel an uncomfortable urge or sensation that something needs to be done, even if you can’t quite explain why?

No, doc, it's not like that. I don't get any weird urge that something just has to be done. It's really just me eating. 

Although, talking about things that just have to be done... I finally got around to cleaning out the gutters this weekend. I've been putting it off since last fall, and man, they were completely packed with leaves and pine needles. We have this massive oak tree in the front yard, and it just dumps stuff everywhere. I had to borrow my neighbor's extension ladder because mine is only a six-footer, and there was no way I was reaching the second-story roofline with that. My neighbor, Tom, he's a retired firefighter. Great guy, always has the right tools for everything. His garage looks like a hardware store. He was telling me about his grandson who just started playing little league, and how they bought him this expensive composite bat. I guess the kids don't use aluminum bats as much anymore? I don't know, when I played, it was all aluminum. You'd hit the ball and it would make that loud *ping* sound. My dad used to come to all my games, sit right behind home plate with his folding chair... 

But yeah, anyway, no weird urges or anything before I eat. Just hungry, I guess.

When you're picking at the food in the kitchen, do you ever feel like you have to do it in a certain way, such as eating specific foods first or following a particular pattern, even if you're not sure why?

No, nothing like that. I don't have a system or a pattern or anything. I just eat whatever is there. 

Like I said, usually whatever my wife made. She's actually been trying this new meal prep thing lately, where she cooks everything on Sundays and puts it in these little glass containers. She got a whole set of them on sale at Target. They have those snap-on lids with the rubber gasket so they don't leak, which is great because the plastic ones we used to have were terrible. I took spaghetti to work once in one of those cheap plastic ones, and the lid popped off in my lunch cooler. Red sauce everywhere. It got all over my thermos, my apple, everything. I spent half my lunch break just wiping out the inside of the cooler with paper towels from the breakroom. The paper towels at the warehouse are that really rough brown kind, you know? Like sandpaper. They don't absorb anything, they just kind of push the mess around. I told the office manager we need better paper towels, but she just rolled her eyes at me. 

But no, to answer your question, I don't have to eat the food in any special order or anything. I just grab it and eat it.

Well, it's... it's definitely not relief. I mean, maybe for like a split second when I first start, but mostly it's just really frustrating. It's exactly like you said, completely out of my control. And then I just feel awful about myself afterward. 

It's sort of like... well, speaking of feeling awful, did I mention they changed the break room coffee at work? Used to be this decent dark roast, kept you going through the graveyard shift. Well, work is... work is fine. I'm still getting to all my shifts at the warehouse, handling the inventory, not missing any time. I swear, if I have to sit behind another gravel truck going ten miles an hour... 

But, uh, where was I? Oh, right, the food thing. Yeah, so work is okay, but at home... it's getting a little weird. My sister and her kids are staying with me right now, and usually we all hang out in the kitchen late, playing cards or whatever. But lately, I've just been... avoiding it. I'll make an excuse and go to my room because I'm just so on edge around the food, and I'm terrified one of them is going to notice how uneasy I am. My nephew, Leo, he's a smart kid, he notices everything. Last week he asked me why I was staring at the pantry door. Kids, right? They just say whatever pops into their head. Reminds me of when I was his age, I used to ask my dad why he was going bald, which he did not appreciate. But yeah, I'm just trying to stay out of the kitchen when people are around so they don't see how weird I'm acting.

My buddy Mike—the one who almost drove the forklift into the office—he actually threw his hat at the TV. I told him, 'Mike, you're gonna break the plasma, and Gary's not paying us enough to replace that.' 

But anyway, yeah, I'm not feeling down or losing interest in things. I still like my weekends, even if the football is terrible right now. It's really just this... this whole food thing at night that's bothering me. Everything else is pretty much normal.

patient.answer:
No, not really. I don't feel any weird build-up or anything like that. It's not like an itch I have to scratch, you know? It's just... I'm there, and then it's happening. 

Speaking of scratching an itch, though, my dog Buster has been driving me up the wall lately. He's this Golden Retriever mix, right? Great dog, usually super chill. But the last couple of weeks, he's been scratching at the back door non-stop. Like, all night long. Scratch, scratch, scratch. I thought maybe he had fleas or something, but the vet said he's clean. Turns out, there's this raccoon that's been getting into the trash cans behind the garage. Huge thing, looks like it's been eating better than half the guys at the warehouse. Mike saw it the other day when he came over to watch the game and he swore it was a small bear. But yeah, Buster just sits there at the glass door, whining and pawing at it because he wants to go out and get the raccoon. It's driving me crazy. Steve spent four hours staring at the hydraulic lift, drank three of my Mountain Dews out of the breakroom fridge, and then told us we just needed to let it warm up longer in the mornings. doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences any awareness or belief that the behavior is inappropriate or unwanted, and if there's any attempt to resist or suppress it.

target_item.manifestation: What worries me is that once I start picking at the food late at night, I tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' but my hand keeps going back like I don't get to make the decision anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient tries to stop himself from eating, which directly relates to the feeling of a lack of control over eating during the episode.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I definitely feel like I shouldn't be doing it. That's the part that really worries me. Because once I start picking at the food in the kitchen, I'll literally tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago, time for bed,' but my hand just keeps going back. It's like I don't even get to make the decision anymore, you know? 

It's kind of like how Gary is about the overtime schedule at work. He says he's making the schedule, but really, his wife is the one pulling the strings. She comes into the office on Thursdays—always wearing these loud, clanky bracelets—and suddenly all the shifts are changed around. Last Thursday, she completely messed up my weekend rotation. I was supposed to have Saturday off to go to my niece's quinceañera. My sister went all out for it, rented this huge hall down by the river. They even had a chocolate fountain, which honestly sounded like a disaster waiting to happen with all those kids running around. I told my sister, 'Maria, you're gonna be cleaning chocolate off those rented chair covers for a week.' But anyway, Gary's wife just crossed my name right off the Saturday off-list. I had to threaten to use my sick days just to get out of there by three. 

But yeah, with the food, I try to stop. I tell myself to stop. But it's like my hand has a mind of its own and just keeps grabbing more.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences the onset of eating episodes during sleep, which would help distinguish between Night Eating Syndrome (F51.3) and other candidates.
doctor.question: Do you ever wake up in the middle of the night and realize you're eating without being fully aware of it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about sleep-related eating disorder (waking up and eating without full awareness). This is not covered by any of the binge eating disorder symptom profiles provided, which involve eating while awake with a sense of loss of control, not during sleep.

patient.answer:
No, I'm definitely awake. I mean, I know what I'm doing, I just... I can't seem to stop it once it starts. But I'm not sleepwalking or anything like that. 

My cousin Hector used to sleepwalk when we were kids. It was the craziest thing. He'd get up out of bed, eyes wide open but just totally blank, you know? One time, we were staying at our abuela's house for the summer, and he got up in the middle of the night, walked right past me on the top bunk, went down the hall, and started trying to unlock the front door with a spoon. A spoon! My abuela heard the rattling and came out with her broom, thinking someone was trying to break in. She almost whacked him over the head before she realized it was just Hector in his Spider-Man pajamas. After that, she started putting a chair in front of the door at night. She said it was for the sleepwalking, but I'm pretty sure she was just paranoid about the neighborhood. It was changing a lot back then. A lot of new families moving in, the old bakery on the corner closed down... man, they had the best pan dulce. You could smell it from three blocks away on a Sunday morning. 

But yeah, no, I'm awake when I'm in the kitchen. I don't wake up mid-chew or anything. I'm fully aware I'm doing it, even if I feel like I can't stop.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning due to the eating behavior, which would help differentiate between candidates like Night Eating Syndrome (F51.3), Binge Eating Disorder (F50.00), and Adjustment Disorder with Disturbance of Conduct (F43.20).

patient.answer:
Well, it doesn't really affect my work. I mean, I'm still getting to all my shipping and receiving shifts on time and handling my responsibilities. You know, unloading the trucks, doing the inventory counts. Even with Gary breathing down my neck about the new barcode scanners. He bought these cheap scanners online instead of going through the corporate vendor, and half the time they don't even read the labels. I told him, 'Gary, you're trying to save a buck, but it's costing us hours in manual entry.' And don't even get me started on the battery life. You leave one off the charger for ten minutes and it's dead. Last Tuesday, I had a whole pallet of wiper blades sitting on the dock for an hour because I had to keep swapping out scanners. It's ridiculous. 

But, um, at home... yeah, it's starting to mess with things a little. I've actually started avoiding some of the late family time in the kitchen. Usually, my wife and kids will hang out there after dinner, maybe have some tea or something, but I just... I don't want to be in there. I'm worried someone will notice how uneasy I am around the food, you know? Like they'll see me eyeing the leftovers or getting anxious about it. So I just make an excuse and go watch TV in the other room.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's behavior is associated with a sense of guilt, shame, or self-criticism that might suggest a mood disorder or exacerbate the existing behavior.

patient.answer:
Oh, absolutely. The guilt is... it's a lot. I really don't like anyone seeing how much I put away, so I always wait until my aunt and the rest of the house are completely asleep, and I try to keep it as quiet as possible in the kitchen. 

My aunt actually just moved into our spare room downstairs a few months ago, and she is such a light sleeper. She leaves her door cracked open because of her little dog, Chico. He's this tiny Chihuahua mix that just shakes all the time, you know the type? My brother-in-law had to give him to us because his new landlord was super strict about no pets. That landlord was a real piece of work, actually. He tried to keep my brother-in-law's entire security deposit, claiming the dog ruined the carpets, but man, those carpets were from like 1992. They had that terrible green and pink floral pattern that everyone used to have in their dining rooms back in the day. I told him he should take the guy to small claims court, but he said it wasn't worth the filing fee and taking time off work. 

But anyway, Chico barks at the drop of a hat, so I have to be like a ninja with the pantry and the fridge door. If the rubber seal on the fridge makes that loud popping sound when it opens, I just freeze and hold my breath. I just... I'd be so incredibly embarrassed if she or my wife walked in and saw all the wrappers on the counter.

No, I don't think so. It's not like a pressure or an urge like that. I just... I go in there and start eating. It's not this big buildup or anything. 

Speaking of pressure, though, the tire pressure light in my truck has been driving me crazy all week. It's a 2014 Silverado, and I swear those sensors are just designed to break. I took it to the gas station down the street—the one on Elm, with the really good breakfast tacos in the back? Man, the lady who makes the salsa there, she doesn't mess around. It's got this smoky flavor, maybe chipotle or something, and it will clear your sinuses right out. I try to get there before 7:00 AM on my way to the warehouse, otherwise the line is out the door with all the construction guys working on that new apartment complex over by the highway. They're throwing those buildings up so fast, it makes you wonder about the quality, you know? Like, are the walls just paper-thin? 

But yeah, I filled all four tires, checked them with my own gauge, and the stupid light on the dashboard is still on. My buddy Dave says I just need to reset the computer, but I don't want to mess with the battery terminals and end up locking out my radio. That happened to him, and he had to drive around in silence for a month until he found the factory code in his glovebox. 

But no, to answer your question, there's no weird physical urge or anything before I eat. I just do it.

No, like I was saying, it's really not like that. There's no pressure or discomfort or anything demanding I do it. I just... I just go to the kitchen and eat. I don't really know how else to explain it. 

But man, talking about discomfort, I slept on my neck wrong two nights ago, and I have had this knot right at the base of my skull that will not quit. My wife told me I need to get one of those contoured memory foam pillows, but I don't trust them. We bought a memory foam mattress topper a few years ago, supposedly infused with cooling gel, right? Spent like two hundred bucks on it at Bed Bath & Beyond before they closed down the one near the mall. Which is a shame, by the way, because that plaza is just dying now. The anchor store is empty, the pretzel place is gone, and the only thing left is a discount shoe store and a cell phone repair kiosk. It's depressing to drive by. 

Anyway, that mattress topper was like sleeping on a giant marshmallow that trapped all your body heat. I woke up sweating every single night in November. I finally rolled it up and shoved it in the hall closet, and it's been taking up half the space in there ever since. But yeah, no, I don't get any weird internal pressure before I eat. I just start eating.

Well, apparently, their supplier sent the wrong size vents for an entire floor, and the general contractor is threatening to hold their payment. It's a huge mess. He was asking if I knew anyone at my warehouse who could source the right parts faster, but our inventory is completely different. We mostly handle industrial fasteners and heavy-duty shelving units. You wouldn't believe how heavy some of those pallets are. Last week, the forklift driver, Gary—great guy, but a little careless sometimes—he clipped the edge of a rack, and I thought the whole aisle was going to come down like dominoes. Luckily, it just dented the support beam, but the safety manager had a complete meltdown. We had to sit through a two-hour safety refresher in the breakroom, and the AC in there has been broken since July. 

But yeah, no, I don't eat to relieve any weird thoughts or feelings. It's just eating.

She completely freaked out, dropped the recycling bin right there on the concrete. There were cans everywhere. We usually take the cans down to the recycling center on Saturdays because they actually pay you a few cents a pound for aluminum, and it adds up, you know? Last year we saved enough from just cans to buy a new gas grill for the patio. It's a Weber, really nice one, three burners. We had the neighbors over for burgers a couple of weekends ago to break it in. 

But anyway, she's screaming about this spider, and I had to go out there with a broom. I'm not really a bug guy myself, but you gotta do what you gotta do. I ended up just sweeping it out the side door into the bushes. Hopefully it stays out there. But yeah, to get back to what you were asking... no, there's no physical feeling before I eat. Well, it's usually just in one go, you know? Like, within an hour or two. I'll get home from work, and on some nights, I can go through several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, some tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are left over. And I'm just standing there in the kitchen, like I'm just cleaning up the leftovers, right? 

But speaking of leftovers, my wife makes the best pozole. She uses this specific kind of hominy she gets from the Mexican market two towns over. The one near us closed down during the pandemic, which really sucked because they had this amazing bakery inside. You could get fresh pan dulce every morning. I used to stop there on my way to the warehouse and grab a concha and a coffee. Gary, the forklift driver I mentioned? He used to beg me to bring him those little pig-shaped cookies they made. What are they called... marranitos, yeah. He loved those things. He's actually retiring next year, Gary is. Moving down to Florida to live near his daughter. I don't know how he's gonna handle the humidity down there, honestly. The warehouse gets hot, sure, but Florida is a whole different beast. 

But yeah, anyway, the eating thing... it's just in that one chunk of time, standing in the kitchen. I don't keep waking up all night to do it.

I've been putting it off since last fall, and man, they were completely packed with leaves and pine needles. We have this massive oak tree in the front yard, and it just dumps stuff everywhere. I had to borrow my neighbor's extension ladder because mine is only a six-footer, and there was no way I was reaching the second-story roofline with that. My neighbor, Tom, he's a retired firefighter. Great guy, always has the right tools for everything. His garage looks like a hardware store. He was telling me about his grandson who just started playing little league, and how they bought him this expensive composite bat. I guess the kids don't use aluminum bats as much anymore? I don't know, when I played, it was all aluminum. You'd hit the ball and it would make that loud *ping* sound. My dad used to come to all my games, sit right behind home plate with his folding chair... 

But yeah, anyway, no weird urges or anything before I eat. Just hungry, I guess.

She got a whole set of them on sale at Target. They have those snap-on lids with the rubber gasket so they don't leak, which is great because the plastic ones we used to have were terrible. I spent half my lunch break just wiping out the inside of the cooler with paper towels from the breakroom. The paper towels at the warehouse are that really rough brown kind, you know? Like sandpaper. They don't absorb anything, they just kind of push the mess around. I told the office manager we need better paper towels, but she just rolled her eyes at me. 

But no, to answer your question, I don't have to eat the food in any special order or anything. I just grab it and eat it.
